quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026, consolidated, K-IFRS, reviewed by Samjong KPMG): revenue KRW 141,201M vs KRW 83,343M in H1 2025 (+69.4%); gross profit KRW 69,677M (49.3% GM); operating profit KRW 44,937M (31.8% margin) vs KRW 20,704M (+117%); net income KRW 39,992M vs KRW 18,383M; basic EPS KRW 1,911 vs 896. Q2 2026 alone: revenue KRW 72,929M vs KRW 51,659M in Q2 2025 (+41.2% YoY) and KRW 68,272M in Q1 2026 (+6.8% QoQ); OP KRW 21,320M (29.2% margin) vs KRW 13,713M (+55.5%); net income KRW 19,393M. FY2025 reference: revenue KRW 220,195M / OP KRW 60,054M. Operating cash flow KRW 38,835M (vs 19,132M); cash KRW 78,085M plus KRW 280,000M of short-term financial instruments; zero borrowings after the KRW 20,000M exchangeable bonds were fully exchanged on 2026-04-01; debt-to-equity 12.0%. MIX (consolidated): test-socket products KRW 118,161M = 83.7%, test parts/equipment merchandise KRW 21,704M = 15.4%, services/other KRW 1,336M = 0.9%. Filing tables (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025): memory 22% / non-memory 78% (was 11% / 85%); AI 81% / non-AI 19% (was 67% / 33%); within AI: AI compute (CPU, GPU, ASIC, CPO) 81%, AI memory (HBM, SOCAMM) 9% (nil a year ago), on-device AI 9%, physical AI (humanoid CPU/AP/SoC) 1%; by application: data center 75% (was 64%), smartphone 20%, PC/notebook 3%, automotive 2%. GEOGRAPHY (H1 2026 vs H1 2025): US KRW 43,302M (vs 26,768M), Korea KRW 42,427M (vs 25,290M), Taiwan KRW 20,155M (vs 16,074M), China KRW 4,644M (vs 2,623M), other KRW 30,674M (vs 12,589M); exports 85% of gross sales (KRW 148,882M of 174,925M pre-elimination). Segments pre-elimination: manufacturing (ISC + ISC VINA) revenue KRW 167,583M / OP KRW 41,707M; brokerage (ISC International, Tech Dream) KRW 7,342M / OP KRW 2,871M. Q2 commentary: legacy-memory orders were a one-off that diluted margin, with higher-value SOCAMM2/HBM orders expected to lift profitability from Q3; non-memory CPU demand more than doubled (+100% YoY) on hyperscaler data-center investment, and AI accelerator/ASIC orders are expected to rise sharply.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 rev KRW 141.2B (+69.4% YoY); Q2 rev KRW 72.9B (+41.2% YoY, +6.8% QoQ); Q2 OP KRW 21.3B (29.2%); AI 81% of sales, data center 75%; US KRW 43.3B / Korea 42.4B / Taiwan 20.2B

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and customers (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): ISC carries no order backlog table because it builds to order — standard products ship within 10 days of the purchase order, special orders within 2-4 weeks; contract liabilities rose to KRW 937M from KRW 215M at year-end. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (>=10% of consolidated H1 revenue): customer A KRW 19,801M (14.0%; KRW 15,733M a year ago) and customer B KRW 15,622M (11.1%; KRW 3,822M a year ago, 4.1x). Customer B's figure equals the related-party sales to SK HYNIX disclosed in the notes: KRW 15,622M in H1 2026 (Q2 alone KRW 7,960M) vs KRW 3,822M in H1 2025, plus KRW 516M to SK hynix Semiconductor (Chongqing); receivables from SK Hynix KRW 14,381M at 2026-06-30. Domestic sales go direct to 'Samsung Electronics, Hynix and others' plus equipment/parts makers; ~300 customers worldwide, with VIP accounts spanning the three global memory IDMs, North American CPU/GPU/mobile-SoC fabless, Korean and North American AI-chip fabless, Taiwanese/Chinese mobile fabless, automotive-chip customers and big tech. Q2 order flow: system-level-test sockets won for a North American customer's H2 2026 flagship smartphone; AI-PC CPU and AI-accelerator development projects expected to lift the PC line from H2; equipment/materials orders (co-developed module testers, high-speed burn-in testers, chemicals) grew with the captive customer, whose HBM cleaning chemicals and memory-module PCBs drove H1, and H1 orders tied to the captive customer's Yongin cluster (chemicals, EFEM, memory-module PCB) start shipping in H2; equipment lead times mean Q1 orders book as Q2/Q3 revenue. SKC provides a KRW 1,100M performance guarantee on a customer supply-purchase contract.
quarterly_data.figure: Customer A KRW 19.8B (14.0%), customer B / SK Hynix KRW 15.6B (11.1%, 4.1x YoY); no backlog table (10-day / 2-4 week lead times); contract liabilities KRW 0.9B

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): H1 2026 production output 12,066K units (test sockets 2,671K, pogo pins 9,395K) vs 15,416K for all of FY2025 and 15,048K in FY2024, at the Seongnam and Ansan plants in Korea and the Hanoi (Vinh Phuc) plant of ISC VINA in Vietnam; capacity is stated to vary with working days, headcount and skill for small-lot, multi-product build-to-order production. PP&E additions KRW 5,774M in H1 (cash capex KRW 7,773M vs KRW 1,784M in H1 2025), construction-in-progress KRW 2,661M (vs 1,661M); ISC VINA alone spent KRW 9,324M on investing activities in H1. Board resolutions: 2026-03-05 approved a pogo-socket production-line expansion; 2026-04-28 approved an additional lease of the SKC Suwon research centre; 2026-05-26 approved a Songdo site expansion and consolidated-relocation plan. KRW 158,700M of the October 2023 rights-issue proceeds remains in term deposits, earmarked for 'semiconductor portfolio expansion - domestic / Vietnam fab expansion investment'. Raw materials (silicone, conductive powder, etc.) purchases KRW 48,665M in H1; the elastomer and conductive powder are produced in-house and gold prices are the main input-cost risk. Market: the 2026 global test-socket market is expected to grow ~10%; commodity (non-HBM) memory sockets began a gradual recovery in Q2 2026 and AI-led non-memory is growing double digits; server DRAM and mobile DRAM socket orders have been rising since Q2 on major memory customers' capacity additions.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 output 12,066K units; PP&E additions KRW 5.8B (cash capex KRW 7.8B, 4.4x YoY); pogo-socket line expansion (03-05-2026) and Songdo site expansion (05-26-2026) approved; KRW 158.7B earmarked for Korea/Vietnam fab expansion

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline and Q3 2026 outlook (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): (1) 'ISC Link-Edge', a next-generation AI-server interface socket launched in H1 2026 for validating high-speed connections between CPU, GPU, ASIC, memory, networking and storage inside one system, begins initial mass-production supply to a global data-center infrastructure solution customer, with revenue expected to grow strongly from 2027 - the filing frames it as ISC expanding from a test-socket maker into an AI data-center test-infrastructure company; (2) initial supply of SOCAMM2 and HBM4 test solutions started in Q2 2026, to be supplied turnkey (socket plus tester), with SOCAMM2 / HBM4 / HBM4E test-solution revenue ramping from Q3; (3) agentic-AI demand is expected to keep server-CPU and AI-PC CPU demand rising in Q3; (4) captive-customer new-fab ramp lifts chemicals and EFEM first, then testers and memory-module PCBs ahead of mass production. R&D spend KRW 7,416M in H1 (5% of sales, FY2025 KRW 14,176M); 451 registered patents and 72 pending; R&D themes include LPDDR 0.2-0.3mm-pitch high-speed silicone-rubber sockets, 150C burn-in silicone sockets, high-frequency and fine-pitch (<0.5mm) conductive-rubber contactors, probe-card interposers and pin-plus-rubber hybrid sockets. Corporate: the KRW 20,000M 1st/2nd exchangeable bonds (5% coupon, due 2027-03-09) were fully exchanged on 2026-04-01 with 678,259 treasury shares delivered; SKC raised its stake to 48.49% (10,279,137 shares) by exercising a call option on 734,490 shares on 2026-03-05 and Helios No. 8 PEF exited; the co-CEO structure ended on 2026-03-26 with Kim Jung-ryeol as sole CEO and Cho Dong-il as board chair; FY2025 dividend KRW 850/share (KRW 17,395M) paid; auditor changed to Samjong KPMG for 2026-2028; a KRW 7,402M construction-cost claim by Hanwha over the head-office building is in first-instance litigation; corporate credit rating AA (e-Credible, 2025-04-24).
quarterly_data.figure: ISC Link-Edge AI-server interface socket: initial mass supply to a global DC-infrastructure customer, growth from 2027; SOCAMM2/HBM4/4E turnkey test solutions ramp from Q3 2026; R&D KRW 7.4B (5%); 451 patents
